items.reason: The githooks half was already closed (versioned .githooks/ auto-installed by every just recipe, with server-side commit-lint in CI), so the open half is branch protection — which no worktree can enable; I versioned the rule as .github/branch-protection.json, added a CI-run gate that keeps its required-check names matching the workflows (it caught two names CODEOWNERS already had wrong), and a one-command `just protection-apply`, but a maintainer with admin rights still has to run it.

Pinning needs a network round trip to resolve each tag to a commit SHA and inventing one would break the workflow; the second half of the item (wire `just pin-check` into CI as a gate) was already done before this cycle — scripts/ci/pinned-actions.mjs runs in the `Ship inventory` job with a ceiling of 33 that exactly equals today's floating count, so it already blocks anything new.

Added CONTRIBUTING.md covering setup and the auto-installed hooks, the verify loop and the repo's 0/2/3-exit-code convention, the conventional-commit rule, the required checks by their exact GitHub names, branch protection, releases, and the four edits that add a second maintainer; linked from README.md, CLAUDE.md and .ai/manifest.yaml.

lessons: In this repo a guardrail is only considered real if something can observe it going RED: every instrument under scripts/ci/ ships with a *.test.mjs fixture suite, uses exit codes 0 clean / 2 findings / 3 CANNOT-CHECK, and reconciles its register against the tree in BOTH directions. Match that shape when adding a gate here, or it will read as decoration.

Required-check lists rot invisibly. This repo's CODEOWNERS named `test` and `Ship inventory + doc-sync` — but a matrix job reports `test (ubuntu-latest)` / `test (windows-latest)` and the job had been renamed, so two of six names would have matched nothing. When a scan says branch protection is unverifiable, the closable half is usually keeping the declared check names reconciled with the workflow jobs.

Scanners under-report guardrails that are implemented without the canonical config filename: this repo's pre-commit hooks live in .githooks/ (auto-installed via core.hooksPath) and its commit-message rule is a 200-line node script, so `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `commitlint.config.js` are both absent while both controls actually operate. Check for the practice before adding the file.
